task.agent_directive: Investigate Micron's high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and data-center memory revenue driven by AI demand, with cited figures.
constraints: Cite a source for every financial figure you record.
Use the most recently reported fiscal periods.
Focus on HBM and data-center memory.
success_criteria: Report HBM or data-center revenue figures for recent quarters

events.content:
Micron did not disclose a stand-alone total HBM-revenue figure for fiscal Q3 2026; it did disclose that it had already shipped **more than $1 billion of HBM4 revenue**, while HBM4 12-high’s volume ramp was running about twice as fast as the prior HBM3E 12-high ramp. [[1]] 

The broader AI-memory read-through was exceptionally strong: fiscal Q3 revenue was **$41.46 billion**, including record DRAM revenue of **$31.3 billion** (76% of sales, +67% sequentially) and NAND revenue of **$9.9 billion** (+99% sequentially). [[2]] [[3]] 

Data-center revenue exceeded **$25 billion** in the quarter—an annualized run rate above $100 billion—and data-center SSD revenue exceeded **$5 billion**, more than doubling sequentially. [[3]] 

Management attributed the tight market to AI-driven demand, saying DRAM and NAND industry demand continued to significantly exceed supply and that it expected tight conditions to persist beyond calendar 2027. [[3]] 

The demand outlook also strengthened because Micron raised its calendar-2026 server-unit-growth expectation to the **high-teens percentage range**, citing agentic AI’s expansion of memory needs beyond accelerator racks into CPU and storage infrastructure. [[3]] 

For forward visibility, Micron said it had entered 16 strategic customer agreements, with approximately **$100 billion** of remaining performance obligations for agreements signed through and after fiscal Q3, although it cautioned that RPO is based on minimum committed volumes/prices and is not a forecast of total revenue. [[3]] 

In short, the reported **>$1 billion HBM4 figure** confirms a rapid early ramp, while the much larger data-center, DRAM, pricing, supply-tightness, and contracted-demand disclosures indicate that AI demand was the central driver of Micron’s fiscal-Q3 surge rather than HBM alone. [[1]] [[3]]

Sources:
[S1.1] Financial results - Micron Investor Relations — https://investors.micron.com/static-files/2354ecda-77a0-4ddd-8462-a631eb491356
[S1.2] Micron Technology, Inc. - Micron Technology, Inc. Reports Record Results for the Third Quarter of Fiscal 2026 — https://investors.micron.com/news/press-release/2026/Micron-Technology-Inc--Reports-Record-Results-for-the-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-2026/default.aspx
[S1.3] Micron Technology, Inc. Fiscal Q3 2026 Earnings Call Prepared Remarks — https://investors.micron.com/static-files/631b1a32-5537-46ae-8f40-82e42fc79dfe
